<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fb9c22aa0929e19ae76707cb55b5f24fead2d9fe` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `868f4c236c858e577478b59d290e864683de64d9` — the merge of head `362cd23e347656b16b605a7af60b5aeb88706e3e` into base `fb9c22aa0929e19ae76707cb55b5f24fead2d9fe`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 868f4c236c858e577478b59d290e864683de64d9 && git checkout 868f4c236c858e577478b59d290e864683de64d9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fb9c22aa0929e19ae76707cb55b5f24fead2d9fe 362cd23e347656b16b605a7af60b5aeb88706e3e && git checkout -B drift-repro fb9c22aa0929e19ae76707cb55b5f24fead2d9fe && git merge --no-ff 362cd23e347656b16b605a7af60b5aeb88706e3e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fb9c22aa0929e19ae76707cb55b5f24fead2d9fe
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fb9c22aa0929e19ae76707cb55b5f24fead2d9fe` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

This PR edits no `packages/core` file, but `test:repo` holds the six core pins that read sources outside the package (`vitest.repo-tests.json`). Among them are `row-serving-door-exposure.pin.test.ts` and `second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts`, which both scan `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`. The likeliest path is a scan over `resolveFormulaRelated`'s new `referenceTargetOf` / `_registry.getObject` read. That is not measured: the job log's download is refused from this seat, so the assertion is not in hand.

The job log is behind a host this session cannot reach (proxy 403); the cause below is read off the pin's own source against the diff, not off the log.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The refusal, as implemented** (`refuseUndeclaredHopField`, validate-expressions.ts 1962–2003, called from `judgeFieldFormula` after `refuseStoredMetadataBodyHop`) — RIGHT in mechanism. For each `record.FIELD.COLUMN` traversal the analyser reports, it takes the carrying object's authored field `FIELD` (`fieldEntries(obj)`), asks `referenceTargetOf(def)` for the target, skips a stored-metadata-body target (owned by `refuseStoredMetadataBodyHop`, not judged twice) and a target `fieldIndex` has no entry for, then refuses each column that is neither `id` nor in `fieldIndex.get(target)`. "Declared" is therefore `buildFieldIndex`'s set: the target's authored field names (either `fields` shape) plus `injectedColumnsFor(obj)` = `resolveInjectedSystemColumns(obj).names` (the primary key, `organization_id` when tenancy applies, the audit provenance family, `owner_id` / `owning_business_unit_id` by ownership tier), plus `id` again. The runtime loader's "declared" (`undeclaredRelatedFields`, engine.ts 2677) is the registry object's `fields` keys plus `id`, and `applySystemFields` (registry.ts 526) spreads exactly that plan's columns into `fields`. The two sets coincide, so the lint refuses only what the loader would answer `undeclared-field` — the set of formulas that read null on every row today.

2. **Can a formula that works today be refused?** Judged per case:
   - an injected column on the target (`record.book.created_at`, `record.book.owner_id`): admitted — pinned (`created_at`) and derived from the same plan the registry injects. One over-inclusion in the safe direction: the lint derives without the deployment's `platformGlobalObjects`, so `organization_id` stays admitted on a platform-global target where the runtime does not inject it; a missed catch, never a refusal;
   - a field contributed by an `extend` contributor or an `objectExtensions` body: **at the save door, admitted.** The door's universe is `registry.listItems('object')` → `getAllObjects` → `resolveObject(fqn)`, the fold of every extender over the base (registry.ts 4170–4262), narrowed by `narrowObjectsToPackageClosure` (runtime-gate.ts 416) to system objects, unpackaged overlay rows, the written package and its declared dependencies; the written item replaces its stored self (`buildRuntimeWriteSnapshots`). The target's field map at the door is the same merged map the loader reads. **At `os build` / `os validate` the lint folds nothing** (no `objectExtensions` handling in validate-expressions.ts, none in the CLI's stack assembly), so in a multi-package stack that carries BOTH the target's owner object AND an extension adding the field, a formula reading that extended field is refused at build although it computes at runtime. This is the same gap the first-segment existence check already has (a formula reading its own object's extension-contributed field is "unknown field" at build today), now extended one hop; the lint's own ledger states the stance ("Object extensions are not judged", validate-field-consumers.ts 167). Narrow, build-time only, not the card's door. Flagged in ③.5, not blocking;
   - a target declared in another package of the closure: judged at the door (limb 4), pinned (`runtime-gate.object-formula-writes.test.ts`, `fx_book` from `com.example.library`); at build, carried only if the stack carries it, else not judged;
   - a system object target: carried at the door unconditionally (limb 1); `sys_user` declares `name`, `email`, `image` and the rest (sys-user.object.ts 729 ff.), so `record.assignee.name` through a `user` field (implicit target `sys_user`, `IMPLICIT_REFERENCE_TARGETS`) is admitted;
   - a target the snapshot does not carry: not judged (`fieldIndex.has(target)` false) — pinned (`hop_elsewhere`). Right: a missed catch, never a false refusal;
   - `reference` by short name: judged; by FQN: `fieldIndex` keys on `obj.name`, so an FQN-spelled reference is not judged (missed catch). The spelling of the carrier (`reference` vs legacy) is `referenceCarrierOf`'s, shared with the runtime;
   - case or label forms of a column: refused, exactly as the loader's `n in declared` refuses them at runtime — nothing working is lost;
   - the hop FIELD itself an injected lookup (`record.owner_id.name`, `record.created_by.email`): `fieldEntries(obj)` lists authored fields only, so not judged — a missed catch (the hop works at runtime: the registry's `owner_id` def is a lookup to `sys_user`). Not a refusal;
   - a `tree` self-reference with no `reference` carrier: `referenceTargetOf` answers undefined before the registry materialises it, so not judged at build and judged against the object's own index at the door. Not a refusal;
   - a field typed other than `lookup` / `master_detail` / `user` / `tree` (`REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES`): `referenceTargetOf` answers undefined, not judged, and the runtime plans no hop for it either.
   Net: the save door newly refuses exactly the formulas whose hop column the loader would mark `undeclared-field`; every refused formula reads null on every row at the merge base. No formula that computes a value is refused at the door.

3. **Code and message** — RIGHT. No new code: the issue goes into the field-formula pass's `issues` list and surfaces under the existing `EXPRESSION_INVALID` rule (`expression-invalid`); the dogfood pin asserts rule `expression-invalid` on the 422 and the door pin asserts `expressionFindings(result.errors)`. The message opens `unknown field \`COLUMN\` on \`TARGET\``, the shared validator's own first-segment words (formula validate.ts 707 and 760), then names the reference read (`record.book`), the target, and where NOT to declare the field. One body for all three doors: `runStackExpressionPasses` is called by `validateStackExpressions` (the CLI's `runAuthoringRules` through authoring-rules.ts 688, for `os validate`, `os build`, `os lint`) and by the runtime gate with `runtimeWriteType: 'object'`, under which `judgeFieldFormula` is not fenced. The `stored` pass (#22118, runtime-gate.ts 674–675) reads only findings located on ANOTHER entry, so a re-save of an object whose stored self already carries the fault is refused too: the WARN's "a re-save of the object refuses it with a located message" is true at this head for this fault, as the dev says, and not only for a first save.

4. **The isolation** (`resolveFormulaRelated`, engine.ts 6287–6333; `formulaHopScope`, 2713–2755) — RIGHT, proven by the diff. `wanted` is built fresh per call from the plan (no plan set is mutated); for each reference the target's registry fields are read and `undeclaredRelatedFields` splits the union; the undeclared columns are deleted from the shared read set and recorded per reference; a reference left with nothing is dropped; the loader then reads only declared columns under `authority: 'caller'`. `formulaHopScope` first intersects THIS formula's own named columns with the reference's undeclared set and, on a hit, returns the `undeclared-field` refusal naming only those columns; otherwise it binds the row as before. Consequences: a valid sibling's read set equals its read set alone (pinned: one `lib_book` read with `fields` `id,title`; booted: `?fields=summary` alone equals the full read); the bad formula reads `null` with its own report; `reportFormulaFault` is untouched, so the dedupe stays once per (object, field) per engine instance; the second-hop marker (`formulaHopReads`) and `hopConflict` entries are untouched. A formula reading only undeclared columns through a reference nobody else reads never reaches `bindings` (the undeclared check returns first), so the dropped reference costs nothing.

5. **The predicate seam** — UNCHANGED, by the diff. `resolvePredicateRelated` (engine.ts 10207) has no hunk; `collectPredicateRelationships` has none; `resolveOneHopRelated`'s only hunk replaces `declaredHere`/`undeclared` with the shared helper, and the two are extensionally identical (`declared` absent → `[]`; else the names that are neither `id` nor `in declared`). The `authority: 'predicate'` branch keeps the whole-reference `undeclared` verdict, which is the out-of-scope finding in ③.9.

6. **The census row** (`federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts`, `engine.ts#resolveFormulaRelated :: referenceTargetOf()` → `caller-predicate`) — RIGHT. `exempt` would be unverifiable (its ASKS claim is a same-site `isFederatedObject` call, and this site makes none); `caller-predicate` is the class the rule-validator's `addReferenceTraversals` and `referenceTraversalConflicts` rows carry for the same kind of use — an author-written expression's own relation path — and its `why` is true: the site reads the registry's field map and no row (the rows are read in `resolveOneHopRelated`, which keeps its own rows).

7. **The pins** — RIGHT and sufficient for the two halves: refusal naming field and target; `id` and `created_at` admitted; an absent target not judged; the door with a cross-package target (LIT and CONTROL); the engine sibling served as alone with one read and only the bad formula reporting; the booted PUT 422 / 200 control / list and findOne values. No pin asserts a value in its title.

8. **What is red, and why it is this diff's** — the `Test Core (2/6)` failure. `packages/core`'s `test:repo` runs the six files of `vitest.repo-tests.json`, among them `src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts`: the `[#22661]` census that `git grep`s every non-test `.ts` under `packages/` for a CALL of `referenceTargetOf` and requires each caller file to have a row in its `CALLERS` ledger (`expect(unclassified).toEqual([])`). This diff adds the import and one code-line call in `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts` (line 1989 at the head; zero calls at the merge base), and no row for that file exists in the ledger — `object-graph.ts`, `validate-field-consumers.ts` and `validate-object-references.ts` each have a `not-a-served-read` row, `validate-expressions.ts` has none. The pin reds on exactly this head and on every head since `d74c110cb1`. The dev's report says `test:repo` was not run locally and the 75 derived gates do not include it; the per-package `lint` and `objectql` suites cannot see a `packages/core` repo pin. The fix is one row (`'packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts': { kind: 'not-a-served-read', reason: 'authoring-time static analysis of metadata; reads no record' }`), which is a new commit and therefore a new head and a new record. A second census note while the file is open: the `engine.ts` row's `also` prose names `referenceExists` and `resolvePredicateRelated` ("the value never served") and nothing of the formula read, which since #24197 serves the related VALUE to the caller through the engine's own `find` without asking the target's API exposure decision. The row passes mechanically (the file is classified), so this is prose drift from #24197, not from this PR — escalated in ③.10.

9. **Public surface.** No export moves in either package; `FormulaRelated` is a module-private type; `undeclaredRelatedFields` is a module-private function; `referenceTargetOf` is already published by `@objectstack/spec`. The card's two targets are met at this head: the save refusal names field and target; one formula's failed read no longer nulls its siblings.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/lint` `minor` with `fix(lint)!:`, `**BREAKING**`, the launch-window sentence, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, the ADR-0087 marker, a FROM → TO and a "What to do" — RIGHT. An accept-set narrowing is breaking; the convention ships it `minor`. Its `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` reason is true: no key, shape or spelling moves; a stored formula with the fault stays stored and reads null as before; the only repair is the author's choice of field, which no `migrate meta` step can make.
- `@objectstack/objectql` `patch` — RIGHT for the code: nothing accepted is refused; a read that served `null` serves the value; the bad formula still reads `null`; the only other observable change is the WARN's attribution. Its ADR-0087 reason is true. **WRONG on the declaration line:** this changeset carries `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, and `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` (`breakingDeclaration`, signal 4) reads the `narrowing` arm as "this changeset declares a breaking change" — so the file reads as breaking at `patch`, which AGENTS.md's own sentence ("`(narrowing)` is BREAKING", shipped `minor` with a carrier) forbids, and the central release notes compiled from changesets would list objectql as breaking when it narrows nothing. No gate catches the pair: the level axis of `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` stands down on a `no` value, and the ADR-0087 gate is satisfied by the marker that is present. The dev's deviation 4 explains it (the dispatch asked for the line in "both changesets"; the honest reading of that ask is the PR's line on the BREAKING changeset, per AGENTS.md's "the changeset body, which also carries the PR's `Clause-②` line"). Correction, on the next head: the objectql changeset's line becomes `Clause-②: no` (no arm) — its marker then is surplus and harmless — and `patch` stands. The PR body's `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is right for the PR, whose narrowing is the lint's.
- Corpus: my census at the head finds 22 `Field.formula` builders in shipped, non-test sources — 7 in examples (app-crm 4, app-showcase 2, app-todo 1) and 15 platform / plugin `display_title`s — and no YAML or JSON formula field; zero of their expressions read `record.X.Y`. The dev's count of 28 differs; the material claim (0 traverse a reference, 0 new refusals in-tree) holds. No example, seed or fixture is refused.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Detached primary checkout and deleted local branch** (deviation 1). Answered, no contract effect: the remote branch is the implementation identity and was pushed empty before any edit; the primary checkout's HEAD state is the worktree protocol's concern (AGENTS.md PD #11), not this record's. The adopting seat may want the primary checkout re-attached to `main`.

2. **Two pin files beyond the claim** (deviation 2). `runtime-gate.object-formula-writes.test.ts` is the same package and the same lane as the declared `validate-expressions.ts`; it pins the declared change at the door and is covered by the declaration's substance, not its letter — a one-line amendment on the `domain:spec` seat posts is the tidy form, not a block. `packages/qa/dogfood/test/formula-hop-undeclared-related-field.dogfood.test.ts` is a new file in a lane the claim did not declare; the dev defers its declaration "to review". ESCALATED to the adopting seat: post the cross-lane declaration to `domain:cli`'s seat post before the queue, as the lint one was posted to `domain:spec`. The Governed Surface Queue Guard is green, so it is not a governed path.

3. **Only the overlap re-run after the second `main` merge** (deviation 3). Answered by the head's check-runs, which ran the whole battery on `313ee1040f`: the overlap the dev chose was right for the merge, and the red that exists is not in the overlap — it is a repo-level census the dev never ran on any head. The lesson for the next head: `packages/core test:repo` is the one suite that sees a new caller of a spec arbiter from any package; run it locally when a diff adds an import of `referenceTargetOf`, `referenceCarrierOf` or the other names its `SEAM_CALLS` list carries.

4. **The `Clause-②` line in both changesets** (deviation 4): the objectql one is the declaration defect in ②; correction owed on the next head.

5. **Build-time refusal of an extension-contributed target field** (①.2, second bullet). Not blocking: the door — the card's seam — is unaffected; the class pre-exists for the first segment; the window needs a stack carrying both the target's owner and its extender. Worth one sentence in the lint changeset's "What to do" ("at `os build`, a target field an `objectExtensions` entry contributes is not visible to this pass"), or a card in the lint lane folding `objectExtensions` into `buildFieldIndex` for every existence verdict at once. Dedupe words: lint field index objectExtensions, build-time unknown field extension-contributed, formula hop extended target field.

6. **Open question 1 (the code family; A taken)** — answered RIGHT: the dispatch's no-new-code rule, the `expression-invalid` rule, and the first- and second-segment verdicts read as one family by their opening words.

7. **Open question 2 (where the isolation lives; A taken)** — answered RIGHT: the measured cause is the formula read's union, and B would have moved rule verdicts on the predicate seam, outside the card's fence. The shared helper is the one reading both seams make of "declared".

8. **Open question 3 (a target the snapshot does not carry; A taken)** — answered RIGHT, and the door's snapshot is as the dev says: the live registry's merged objects plus stored rows, narrowed to system objects, overlay rows, the written package and its declared dependencies (runtime-gate.ts 416, protocol.ts 7373–7420).

9. **Open question 4 (the WARN text; A taken)** — answered RIGHT, with the stronger ground in ①.3: the door's `stored` pass never lets the stored self's own findings cancel, so the re-save the WARN promises is refused, not only a first save.

10. **Out-of-scope finding 1 (the predicate seam's whole-reference `undeclared` verdict for validation rules).** REAL at this head and independent of this PR, by the code: `resolveOneHopRelated` under `authority: 'predicate'` still answers the whole reference `undeclared-field` when any rule's column is undeclared (engine.ts 10346–10349), and the lint's `check` with `traversalHydration` judges a rule condition's hop shape, not its target columns. So one validation rule naming an undeclared related field saves 200 and then every rule through that reference has no verdict, refusing every write with the undeclared message. That is a public write door answering wrongly for the author's other rules (fail-closed, so no disclosure), with a reproducible shape; under PD #10 it meets the filing gate.
